title: aether_converter download job
description: Job consumed by `aether_converter download --job-file <json>`. Authoritative source: crates/aether_converter/src/download.rs (DownloadJob / SubTileSpec).

encoding.description: Elevation PNG encoding (case-insensitive). Any other value fails at runtime.

max_connections.description: Concurrent HTTP connections. Defaults to 256 when absent. The CLI download runs a fixed pool of this many requests; its window is cut 25 % per second only on >= 3 HTTP 429/503 answers in that second (floor max(max_connections / 4, 16)) and grows 10 % per clean second back to this value; timeouts, resets and slow bodies never move it (CONTRACT 9b, changelog 30). On unix, where even a raised open-file limit cannot hold 2 x max_connections + 96 descriptors, it runs (limit - 96) / 2 connections instead and says so (changelog 36). A full run also holds its output files open, one descriptor each, where they fit beside those; elsewhere each write opens its file and says so (changelog 39).

buildings_pbf_dir.description: Directory of {z}_{x}_{y}.pbf vector tiles fused onto the finished .abt tiles as a post-pass. All tiles must share one zoom level. Absent means terrain only.

fetch_bounds.description: Optional fetch region of interest in degrees. Only source tiles intersecting it are downloaded/decoded; pixels outside keep the -9999 void sentinel. Output grid and .abt layout unchanged. Supported by the in-memory downloader only; the file-based `download` CLI rejects jobs carrying it (its sparse writer would read skipped rows as 0 m).

tile_deadline_s.description: Per-source-tile wall-clock cap in seconds across all attempts, back-offs and Retry-After waits; absent = 20 (changelog 30; was 60). At expiry the tile is a `timeout` failure and goes to the parent fill. CLI download only. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.6 (CONTRACT 9b, changelog 28).

repair_source_tiles.description: Source tiles [z, x, y] (z = the job's zoom) to fetch again and patch into the job's EXISTING .abt files; only output pixels wholly determined by listed tiles are rewritten, every other byte is unchanged. Each tile must intersect an output tile and every touched output file must exist, else the run fails before any request. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.6 (older builds ignore it and download the whole job); CONTRACT 9b 'Repair jobs', changelog 28.

cache_dir.description: Directory of the raw source-tile cache, shared by every job, service and zoom that names it, and safe for several converter processes at once. Absent, null or empty: no cache (the run is exactly as without the field). Set: every source tile is looked up in <cache_dir>/<service_key>/z<zoom>/x<x>_y<y div 256>.pack before any request (service_key = the first 16 hex digits of SHA-256(url_template, query string included, + newline + lower-cased encoding), so templates that differ only in their query never share a directory; the informational service.json records the template without its query string, so a key in the query never reaches the disk in clear text - one in the path does); a hit is decoded from the cached bytes without a request, and every HTTP 200 body that decoded and every HTTP 404 the run fetches - the parent fill's coarser tiles included - is written there. Since aether_converter 0.2.9 (changelog 40) a tile without an entry is derived without a request from the cached tiles of up to four finer zooms when they cover it (2 x 2 means in the service's encoding, stored with entry status 3; not the service's own coarser tile). Failed, timed-out, undecodable and degraded tiles are never cached. A directory that cannot be used costs one [Warn] line, never the run. CLI download only (a repair job refetches its listed tiles and rewrites their entries); the in-memory and browser downloaders ignore it. .abt bytes, every parsed line and exit codes are unchanged. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.8 (older builds ignore it); CONTRACT 9b 'Raw source-tile cache', changelog 38.

resolution_m.description: Metres per pixel; writer sets scale = resolution_m / 111111. XYZ samples are area-averaged over each output pixel's footprint (voids excluded from the mean); where a pixel is finer than the source zoom it takes the sample it sits in. See CONTRACT.md section 6.
